key_insight: In linear-elastic homogenization, differentiating a two-local Ising Hamiltonian yields one-local stress observables measurable from the same computational-basis samples as the energy.
engineering_relevance: The formulation extracts homogenized stress directly from an optimized quantum state without reconstructing microscopic displacements or adding measurement bases.
method: Encode the reduced finite-element RVE energy as a QUBO and map it to an Ising Hamiltonian.
Approximate the equilibrium ground state using the variational quantum eigensolver (VQE).
Apply Hellmann–Feynman differentiation with respect to macroscopic strain to construct stress observables.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a demonstration on a two-dimensional periodic RVE but provides no quantitative accuracy, scaling, or hardware-performance results.
watch_item: Finite encoding resolution and approximate VQE convergence can affect equilibrium and stress accuracy; no quantum advantage is established in the abstract.
paper_title: Ising-Encoded Computational Homogenization: Stress as a Quantum Observable
